name: Novus Magnificat
editorial_article:
Released in 1986 on Hearts of Space Records, "Novus Magnificat: Through the Stargate" stands as a monumental achievement in the landscape of new age and space music. Composed by the classically trained musician Constance Demby, the album is widely recognized as a definitive work of the genre, blending the architectural grandeur of Western sacred music with the boundless possibilities of early digital synthesis. The title, Latin for "New Magnificat," signifies Demby's intent to bridge the ancient traditions of the Christian hymn with the contemporary, ethereal textures of the late 20th-century electronic underground.

The album’s creation was a painstaking process that saw Demby transition from initial, intuitive sketches recorded on a 4-track Portastudio to a complex, multi-layered production. Eschewing traditional written scores, she relied heavily on her emotional connection to the music, utilizing instruments like the E-mu Emulator II—a pioneering digital sampler—to conjure symphonic-scale orchestrations, choral swells, and lush electronic atmospheres. With the assistance of co-producer Anna Turner and the sonic contributions of ambient composer Michael Stearns, the work was recorded in sections and woven together into a transformative, long-form experience. "Novus Magnificat" remains a cultural touchstone, having sold over 200,000 copies and earned consistent recognition as one of the most influential ambient albums ever recorded, perfectly embodying the "space music" ethos of sonic expansion and deep, contemplative listening.
